item.description: La física de los agujeros negros está rodeada aún de muchas preguntas sin resolver. Por ejemplo, sabemos que dos agujeros negros pueden fusionarse para dar lugar a uno más grande, ¿pero puede un gran agujero negro dividirse en dos más pequeños? Tradicionalmente se ha pensado que no, pues iría en contra de las leyes de la física. Sin embargo, un equipo de científicos de la Universidad Federico II de Nápoles, la Sorbona de París y la Universidad del Sur de Dinamarca acaba de encontrar un atajo teórico por el que sí sería posible. item.title: Ancient copper mine hints that Iberia played an important role in Bronze Age trade networks
item.description: Copper is essential for making bronze, which shaped tools, weapons and ornaments across Bronze Age Europe. While many Bronze Age mines have been identified throughout Europe, researchers are still trying to pin down which of them were most active at different times and how far their copper traveled. New research, published in the journal Antiquity, suggests that a series of mines in modern-day Spain and Portugal may have been an important source of copper in the Late Bronze Age, with some of that copper ending up as far away as Scandinavia. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Different transcription systems shape chromatin behavior in distinct nuclear regions
item.description: Inside the cell nucleus, DNA is wrapped around histone proteins to form nucleosomes, which are further organized into chromatin. Chromatin has traditionally been divided into transcriptionally active euchromatin and relatively inactive heterochromatin. However, chromatin is not a fixed structure. Nucleosomes continuously move within the nucleus, and this motion is closely related to the physical organization and function of the genome. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Pulling the strings: How stem cells in the developing fruit fly brain organize their DNA from outside the nucleus
item.description: Cells are very particular about the proper locations of their contents. For example, DNA is packaged in the nucleus in a highly specific way, but researchers are still trying to understand how this happens. For stem cells in the brain of a larval fruit fly—a model organism used to study processes such as early development—the DNA is organized so that the center of each strand, called the centromere, is at the top of the nucleus. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Could US midterms impact the EU? Transatlantic ties hit new low after Trump-Putin diesel deal
item.description: From the EU's perspective, the second Trump presidency has felt even more destabilising than the first. From making the false claim that the EU was set up to "screw" the United States, to slapping tariffs on European goods, to making territorial claims on Greenland, to doing a diesel deal with Vladimir Putin and telling Ukraine to get a new president, Donald Trump has more than ruffled feathers on this side of the ocean. He has shaken the very foundations of the historical transatlantic relationship. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: French port strikes: Unions 'will get better working conditions', but can they curb militarisation?
item.description: Carys Garland is pleased to welcome Renaud Foucart, Senior Lecturer at the Department of Economics ECARES at Lancaster University. An international dockworkers’ strike brings into focus the relationship between organized labor, technological change and Europe’s expanding military investment.
